Technology advances at breakneck speed. Yesterday's innovations become today's antiquities. We rush forward, chasing progress, rarely stopping to question whether faster always means better.

Consider the smartphone. A marvel of engineering, certainly. Yet it has fundamentally altered how we interact with reality. We experience life through screens, mediated and filtered. Direct experience becomes increasingly rare.

I conducted an experiment last week. One full day without digital devices. The results were revealing. Initially, anxiety. Then, gradually, a sense of presence I had forgotten existed. The world revealed itself in unexpected ways - textures, sounds, the subtle play of light and shadow that goes unnoticed when your attention is divided.
